_README: Dataset for scripts/eval_retrieval.py.
SHAPE: a JSON LIST of {"query": str, "answerable": bool} -- exactly what
scripts/tune_threshold.py and scripts/eval_responses.py already consume --
plus one extra field, "relevant_ids". Those scripts ignore keys they do not
know about (including this _README), so one file feeds all three.
That is also why this note lives on the first entry instead of a top-level
key: a top-level object would stop being a list and break the other two.
relevant_ids: the row_key of every page/article that genuinely answers the
query. A row_key looks like "page_8219" (or "article_1234" once articles
are ingested) and is written into every chunk's Chroma metadata by
app/rag/ingest.py. It is deliberately the PAGE-level id: a human can judge
"this page answers the question", but not "chunk 3 of this page does".
answerable: true  + non-empty relevant_ids -> those ids SHOULD be retrieved.
answerable: false + empty relevant_ids     -> nothing relevant should
surface; these entries feed
the false-positive rate.
HOW TO FILL IN relevant_ids WITHOUT HAND-HUNTING IDS:
1. Write the query with "relevant_ids": [] and the right answerable flag.
2. Run:  python -m scripts.eval_retrieval --label scripts/my_questions.json
For every entry with an empty relevant_ids it prints the top candidates:
row_key, book/chapter, scores and a text preview, plus a paste-ready
JSON line.
3. Paste the row_keys that actually answer the question. Leave out ones
that are merely on-topic -- a loose gold set inflates recall and hides
real retrieval failures.
4. If NOTHING in the candidate list answers it, either the corpus does not
cover it (set answerable: false, relevant_ids: []) or you have found a
genuine retrieval miss -- in that case grep chroma_dump.csv for the
right page and add its row_key anyway. Those are the most valuable
entries in the set, because they are the ones the metrics must punish.
Aim for 30-50 entries, roughly two thirds answerable. Mix Bengali script,
Banglish and English queries so --ablation can show what the query rewriter
actually buys you.
The row_keys below are real ids from this corpus, labelled with --label,
so the example runs and scores out of the box. Replace them with your own.
